format: pala-1 scitt-bridge statement vector, COSE alg -19
purpose: The published v2 statement and the later published v3 statement, each built again with COSE alg -19 (Ed25519, RFC 9864) in place of -8 (EdDSA). Nothing else changes. A verifier that admits -19 accepts these with the same public key; one that admits only -7 and -8 refuses them as an unsupported algorithm and reads nothing - that is the compatibility, and it runs one way. Real crypto, fake entropy - never use this key outside a test vector.
relation_to_the_other_vectors: scitt-statement-vector.json and scitt-statement-vector-v3.json are unchanged and remain valid. -19 is not a new construction: the content types, the payloads and the protected header's labels are those of v2 and v3. What is extended is the set of values label 1 (alg) may take, from {-7, -8} to {-7, -8, -19}.

key.alg: Ed25519, COSE alg -19 (RFC 9864); the same key the other vectors sign with under alg -8
key.source: RFC 8032, section 7.1, TEST 1 - a published test key, chosen so nothing about it is ours
key.kid_note: RFC 9679 thumbprint of the key: kty, crv and x - not alg. The same under -8 and -19, so a signer that changes identifier keeps its kid.

rules.alg_values: label 1 is -7, -8 or -19; any other value MUST be refused
rules.key_type: -8 and -19 both mean Ed25519 here. A verifier MUST refuse a key that is not Ed25519 under either - Ed448 in particular, which -8 as a family name would otherwise admit - and MUST refuse a key that is not P-256 under -7
rules.what_alg_changes: one signed byte of the protected header. The Sig_structure, the signature algorithm and the verification are those of -8
rules.byte_stability: Ed25519 is deterministic (RFC 8032), so these statements reproduce byte for byte, like the -8 ones

against_the_published_statement.protected_header: identical but for byte 2: 0x27 (alg -8) there, 0x32 (alg -19) here
against_the_published_statement.signature: different - the protected header is signed

against_the_published_statement.protected_header: identical but for byte 2: 0x27 (alg -8) there, 0x32 (alg -19) here
against_the_published_statement.signature: different - the protected header is signed

tamper_expectations: set the alg byte of the protected header back to 0x27 (-8) and keep the signature: verification MUST fail - the protected header is signed, so a statement cannot be relabelled from one identifier to the other
verify with an Ed448 public key: MUST be refused before any signature check - the key is not of the type -19 means
every tamper expectation of the -8 vectors holds unchanged
